Task: Draft a complete business plan for a hypothetical coffee shop.

Business Plan  
Bean There, Brewed That – Artisanal Coffee Shop  

1. Executive Summary  
Bean There, Brewed That (BTBT) will be a 60-seat, neighborhood-focused coffee shop located in the downtown arts district of Riverton (pop. 175,000). BTBT will roast small-batch coffee on-site, pair beverages with locally sourced pastries, and host community events. We seek an initial investment of $275,000 to cover build-out, equipment, pre-opening costs, and working capital. By year 3 we project $835 K in annual revenue, 17 % net margin, and positive cash flow by month 10.

2. Company Description  
Legal form LLC, founded by two partners with ten years’ combined specialty-coffee and hospitality experience.  
Mission To cultivate community through ethically sourced coffee and inclusive gathering space.  
Vision To become Riverton’s “third place” of choice and expand to a second location within five years.  
Values Sustainability, transparency, quality, local collaboration, and diversity.

3. Market Analysis  
Industry U.S. specialty-coffee sales grew 10 % CAGR (IBISWorld). Riverton lacks a roaster-café within a 1-mile radius.  
Target customers 25- to 45-year-old urban professionals, students, and remote workers earning $40 K–$90 K.  
Competitors Three chain cafés (Starbucks, Dunkin’, Big Mug) and two indie shops outside walking distance. BTBT will differentiate with in-house roasting, extended evening hours, and events.  
SWOT  
• Strengths Owner expertise, roaster differentiation, arts-district location.  
• Weaknesses Start-up capital, new brand.  
• Opportunities Rising remote work, demand for experiential retail.  
• Threats Commodity price volatility, potential recession.

4. Products & Services  
Core menu Single-origin pour-overs, espresso-based drinks, cold brew, signature seasonal beverages.  
Food Locally baked pastries, gluten-free and vegan options, light savory toasts.  
Retail Whole-bean coffee, branded merch, brew gear.  
Experiences Roasting classes, latte-art workshops, live music, gallery nights.  
Pricing $3.25 drip, $4.50 latte, $18/12 oz retail bag—positioned at a 15 % premium to chains but below high-end micro-roasters.

5. Marketing & Sales Strategy  
Branding Earth-toned, modern interior; storytelling around origin and roasting.  
Channels Instagram/TikTok, local influencers, weekly email newsletter (loyalty program), Google My Business, community bulletin boards.  
Promotions Grand-opening free cupping sessions; “Mug Club” prepaid membership; student discount 10 %.  
Partnerships Collaborations with the adjacent art gallery, bike co-op, and farmers’ market.  
Sales forecast Daily average 240 transactions year 1, $7.50 average ticket.

6. Operations Plan  
Hours Mon–Thu 6 am–8 pm, Fri 6 am–10 pm, Sat–Sun 7 am–10 pm.  
Site 1,800 sq ft lease ($4,200/mo) with sidewalk patio.  
Equipment 15 kg drum roaster, 2-group espresso machine, grinders, pour-over bar, refrigerated display, POS.  
Suppliers Direct-trade importers (Crop to Cup, Royal Coffee); bakery partnership for daily deliveries.  
Technology Wi-Fi, Square POS, inventory software, energy-efficient HVAC.

7. Management & Personnel  
Co-founder/GM Emma Chen – Q-Grader, former café manager.  
Co-founder/Roaster Luis Moreno – SCA-certified roaster, logistics background.  
Staff 1 assistant manager, 5 full-time baristas, 4 part-time baristas (wage $15/hr + tip share).  
Training 40-hour onboarding; ongoing SCA-aligned modules; quarterly cupping calibration.

8. Financial Plan (Year 1)  
Start-up costs  
• Leasehold improvements $95,000  
• Equipment & installation $110,000  
• Opening inventory $12,000  
• Licenses, legal, insurance $8,500  
• Pre-opening marketing $4,500  
• Working capital (4 mos) $45,000  
Total $275,000  

Funding mix  
• Owners’ equity $80,000  
• SBA 7(a) loan $145,000 at 7 % over 10 yrs  
• Local economic-development grant $50,000 (for façade & equipment)

Projected Income Statement (Year 1)  
Revenue $625,000  
COGS (coffee, food) $160,000  
Gross profit $465,000 (GP margin 74 %)  
Operating expenses $355,000  
EBITDA $110,000  
Less interest & depreciation $60,000  
Net profit $50,000 (8 % NP margin)  

Break-even Monthly sales of $48,500, reached in month 10.  
Cash flow positive Month 10.

Years 2–3 assumptions: 12 % sales growth, stable COGS, modest labor leverage → Year 3 net margin 17 %.

9. Funding Request & Use of Proceeds  
We seek $195,000 in debt/grants to complement $80,000 equity. Funds will be allocated as outlined in start-up costs. Lenders/grantors receive monthly financial statements; SBA note secured by equipment and personal guarantees.

10. Risk Analysis & Mitigation  
Commodity price spikes Use fixed-price forward contracts for 30 % of green coffee.  
Economic downturn Diversify revenue with retail and events; flexible labor scheduling.  
Staff turnover Competitive wages, growth path, benefits (health stipend, paid barista competition fees).  
Regulatory Strict adherence to health, fire, ADA; maintain contingency fund for compliance upgrades.  
Pandemic/health shocks Expand patio, develop online ordering & local delivery for beans and beverages.

11. Milestones & Timeline  
Month 0 Finalize lease, secure permits, order equipment.  
Month 3 Construction complete; start hiring.  
Month 4 Soft opening; feedback loop; adjust SOPs.  
Month 5 Grand opening & marketing blitz.  
Month 10 Break-even/cash-flow positive.  
Year 2 Q2 Launch e-commerce bean subscription.  
Year 3 Q4 Evaluate second-location feasibility.

12. Exit/Expansion Strategy  
If EBITDA > $150 K by Year 4, explore franchising or equity partnership for additional locations. Alternatively, prepare for strategic sale to regional roaster looking for retail footprint.

Appendices  
A. Detailed three-year financial projections  
B. Floor plan & seating map  
C. Sample menus & pricing matrix  
D. Resumés of founders  
E. Letters of intent from bakery and art-gallery partners

Bean There, Brewed That is positioned to capture Riverton’s growing appetite for high-quality, ethically sourced coffee while fostering a vibrant community hub. With experienced leadership, a differentiated on-site roasting concept, and sound financial planning, BTBT offers investors a compelling opportunity for sustainable, profitable growth.
